title: Why OS Virtual Memory Paging Saved LLM Inference: The ChronosPaging advancement in Zig

author: Mateus Yonathan

abstract: We investigate how operating-system virtual memory paging can reduce the memory footprint of large language model (LLM) inference without sacrificing correctness. The ChronosPaging module, implemented in Zig, couples a lightweight page table with a least-recently-used (LRU) replacement policy and a balanced search structure for mapping virtual pages to physical frames. By exploiting the OS's demand paging semantics, the module persists page contents across evictions, enabling inference workloads to operate on a fraction of the model size that would otherwise be resident in RAM. Theoretical analysis shows that page lookups and updates run in $O(\log N)$ time, while the overall memory consumption is bounded by $O(P)$, where $P$ is the number of pages. Formal invariants guarantee that the page table remains height-balanced and key-ordered, ensuring deterministic eviction order. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/zig-systems-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261111_190242_why_os_virtual_memory_paging_s}
